name: List & Enumeration Profiling
description: Examines the structural reliance on bullet points, numbered lists, and rigid sequential transitions (e.g., 'Firstly', 'Secondly', 'Finally'). AI models systematically default to over-structured enumeration to fulfill formatting prompt-tuning, leading to highly predictable, segmented prose compared to organic human writing.
mechanism: Large Language Models (LLMs), particularly those fine-tuned with Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF), are explicitly trained to give helpful, safe, and clearly structured answers. As a byproduct, they lean heavily into extreme structural scaffolding—breaking down almost every explanation into neatly bulleted lists or rigid numerical enumerations. This algorithm scans the text for explicit list markers (Markdown bullets, numbers) and implicit sequential transition markers ('First', 'Furthermore', 'Lastly', 'In conclusion'). It measures the density of these structures relative to the total text volume. Human writers typically deploy lists sparingly, preferring cohesive narrative flow and fluid paragraph transitions to connect ideas. If a text exhibits a near-robotic compulsion to segment its arguments into perfectly balanced, multi-point lists—especially when addressing subjective or narrative prompts where listing is unnatural—it is strongly flagged as structurally artificial.
useCase: Highly effective for auditing cover letters, opinion pieces, and narrative essays where an over-reliance on bullet points and sequential 'First/Second/Finally' structures betrays AI generation.
strengths:
• Targets the core structural bias instilled in commercial LLMs (like ChatGPT or Claude) during RLHF instruction tuning.
• Detects both explicit formatting (bullets) and implicit structural listing (transition words used as list markers).
• Works efficiently across vast amounts of text, relying on clear syntactic markers rather than complex semantic analysis.
limitations:
• Naturally triggers false positives on technical documentation, recipes, resumes, or instructional guides where list-heavy formatting is the human standard.
• Easily bypassed if the user explicitly prompts the AI 'Do not use lists' or 'Write in flowing paragraphs'.
• Requires careful baseline calibration depending on the specific genre of text being analyzed.
parameters:
Analysis: Structural Formatting & Transition Density
Metric: Ratio of Enumerated/Segmented Content vs. Continuous Prose
Output: 0-100 Structural Rigidity (Enumeration Over-reliance) Score
accuracy: Moderate to High — 76-84% accuracy, heavily dependent on the chosen genre. Highly accurate on narrative texts, but drops on inherently structured documents.

references.title: Guo, B. et al. (2023). How Close is ChatGPT to Human Experts? Comparison Corpus, Evaluation, and Detection. NeurIPS.
Wang, Y. et al. (2023). MAGE: Machine-generated Text Detection in the Wild. ACL.
